title: Use EF's asynchronous query adapter intentionally
goal: Choose AsAsyncEnumerable for an EF database query, keep one enumeration per intended query, and release the reader on exit; use this when addressing EF1004 or streaming projected rows.

selectionNotes: EF query behavior; not shared LINQ package migration alone. AsAsyncEnumerable existed before EF11; the new authoring prompt is EF1004.
The historical provider10 comparison does not add a .NET 10 foundation.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: EF Core 11 requires net11.0; no EF11-on-net10.0 route is offered.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared target. Exact recorded SDKs are verification baselines; current-release proof uses RC2, not GA.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Declared sample language mode; no C# 15-only feature is needed.

frameworks: Standalone Microsoft.NET.Sdk console; no web framework requirement

packages.name: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite
packages.reason: Current capability/analyzer verified with 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105; each independent project has CPM pins and a resolved lock file.

packageAssets: EF Core/Relational/SQLite.Core 11 lib/net11.0; Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core lib/net10.0; EF1004 comes from Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Analyzers 11.
providers: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite with actual in-memory SQLite; no external service/account.
Measured native SQLite 3.53.3 with provider10/SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.13; 3.53.4 with provider11/SQLitePCLRaw 3.0.5 plus SQLite package 3.53.4.
platforms: Executed on Windows x64 using the packaged e_sqlite3 native library. Other native OS/architecture routes were not executed.
renderingModes: Not applicable: console/database consumer; no renderer or browser
constraints: EF query behavior; not shared LINQ package migration alone. AsAsyncEnumerable existed before EF11; the new authoring prompt is EF1004.
Neither adapter caches results. Keep the context alive through enumeration; await each operation before reusing it.
SQLite async methods execute synchronously internally: interceptor IsAsync establishes the EF command API path, not nonblocking native I/O or throughput.
The pinned runtime11 ToAsyncEnumerable already returns an IAsyncEnumerable source directly. EF1004 still flags the spelling; do not claim this current EF query always executes synchronously.
prerequisites: Copy every file of the selected project below to one standalone directory. Restore from nuget.org online before running; dependency setup is separate from offline Playbook retrieval.
The open connection owns a disposable in-memory database. Closing it removes sample data; no persistent database or resource is provisioned.
stabilityLimitations: GA-targeted stable contract, measured with .NET 11 RC2 packages/SDK. No experimental API opt-in required; actual GA reconciliation remains outstanding.

sources.title: EF asynchronous query and context lifetime

evidence.scope: Actual EF10 query: ToAsyncEnumerable synchronous commands versus existing AsAsyncEnumerable asynchronous commands; deferred/repeated execution, real reader disposal on break/consumer exception, pre-cancellation.

Actual EF11 query: AsAsyncEnumerable and the pinned runtime11 ToAsyncEnumerable fast path issue asynchronous commands; deferred/repeated execution, real reader disposal on break/consumer exception, pre-cancellation. EF1004 red/green reproduction is separate in eng/Test-EfQueryAdapter.ps1.

humanProof.scope: Automated real SQLite consumers cover these bounded managed/provider claims. No external account, native UI or targeted Human proof is required. Other native platforms, other providers and actual GA remain unverified.
